Daily Briefing — Thursday, September 10 2026

OpenAI mathematical discovery claim meets criticism as Anthropic-backed researchers assert priority; agentic AI moves from pilots to regulated enterprise deployment

AI & Technology

#1 — NYU mathematician accuses OpenAI of racing to preempt Euler proof after Anthropic collaboration — AI Weekly / Scientific American reports

★ Signals competitive tension and model capabilities at platform layer between OpenAI and Anthropic—relevant to enterprise model selection and governance decisions in regulated environments where you deploy AI Content OS

NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge released a Lean-verified proof of finite-time blowup for 3D incompressible Euler equations on September 8, extending prior work. Buckmaster alleges OpenAI accessed rumors of the proof on September 3 and rapidly extended it internally using their model, then offered Buckmaster sole authorship while excluding Alpöge. This marks a turning point in mathematical discovery, positioning AI models as potentially co-discoverers while raising questions about model access to private researcher work.
